Beşiktaş's Europa League game against Israel's Hapoel Be'er Sheva descended into chaos in Batumi, Georgia. UEFA had moved the match out of Istanbul to a neutral venue on security grounds.

Before kickoff, the Beşiktaş players refused to shake hands with the Israeli team. In the stands, Turkish fans raised a Palestinian flag and a banner reading "If you cannot prevent injustice, make it known to everyone." Georgian police moved in to remove the flag and clashes broke out.

Police used batons, tear gas and pepper spray on the Beşiktaş section. One fan was beaten so badly he was left bleeding heavily and taken to hospital. The match was stopped around the 25th minute and the players left the pitch. Clashes continued outside the stadium.

Play resumed at 0–0 after a stoppage of more than 45 minutes. Beşiktaş accused Georgian police of using "disproportionate force" against its supporters, and rival club Galatasaray also condemned the crackdown.

🇪🇺 EU leaders fail to agree on 2028–2034 budget, talks pushed to December

EU leaders ended their special summit in Brussels without a deal on the bloc's next seven-year budget. They also failed to agree on a new €45 billion loan for Ukraine.

European Council President António Costa's compromise puts the budget at around €1.58 trillion, roughly €200 billion less than the European Commission originally proposed. It still satisfies almost no one, often for opposite reasons. The net contributors (Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Austria, Finland and Denmark) want deeper cuts to limit what they pay in. The net beneficiaries in central and southern Europe want more money.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the plan was no basis for agreement because the total was still too high, and ruled out any new joint EU borrowing. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the sides are "light years away" from a solution.

Leaders will try again at the December 17–18 summit.
